issue: Source “How could she help being ‘like that’ to look at?” keeps the accuser's quoted phrase “like that” (her looks as the charge's cause); “Could she help how she looked?” drops the quoted phrase and its ironic distance.
find: Could she help how she looked?
replace: How could she help looking “like that”?

issue: Source “which at once made him gaze and marvel” means immediately; moved to the end, “gaze and marvel at once” reads as ‘simultaneously’.
find: that made him gaze and marvel at once
replace: that at once made him gaze and marvel

issue: Source “She thought she must have been tossed in her perambulator” is passive; “one must have tossed her” introduces an unclear “one” that readers of this edition (where “one”→“you” generic) will take as ‘someone’ rather than a bull.
find: She thought one must have tossed her in her baby carriage when she was tiny.
replace: She thought she must have been tossed in her baby carriage by a bull when she was tiny.

issue: Source “let the Bœuf en Daube overboil” means cook too long (hence the burning smell), not “boil over”.
find: let the Bœuf en Daube boil over?
replace: let the Bœuf en Daube boil too long?

issue: Source hedge “feeling life rather sinister again” is dropped; “sensing again how sinister life was” makes it absolute.
find: sensing again how sinister life was
replace: feeling again that life was rather sinister

issue: Source “her dear Lily, her little Brisk, was a fool” is Mrs. Ramsay's flat verdict on Lily; “was being a fool” softens it to a passing lapse.

Source aside “(as Nancy looked down upon life spread beneath her)” is a parenthesis; the rendering turns it into commas, dropping the paragraph's inner parenthesis (the outer section-long parenthesis is correctly kept).
find: Here and there, as Nancy gazed down at life spread out below, something rose out of the mist
replace: Here and there (as Nancy gazed down at life spread out below) something rose out of the mist
